role_in_parent: This is the central monotonicity step, now isolated cleanly in the coordinate model instead of the false effective-generator model.
statement_nl: Fix integers m >= 2 and g >= 0. Define K_{m,g} to be the set of all tuples k = (k_1,...,k_{m-1}) of positive integers such that: for all integers i,j with 1 <= i <= j <= m-1, if i + j < m then k_i + k_j >= k_{i+j}, if i + j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 >= k_{i+j-m}, and also k_1 + ... + k_{m-1} = g. Then there exists an injective function Phi_{m,g} : K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.

domain_restrictions: indices: i,j ∈ Z with 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1
case 1: if i+j < m then k_i + k_j ≥ k_{i+j}
case 2: if i+j > m then k_i + k_j + 1 ≥ k_{i+j-m}
no explicit condition specified for the boundary case i+j = m
when i+j > m, the index i+j-m lies in {1,...,m-2} (so it is within the defined k-indices {1,...,m-1})
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers m ≥ 2 and g ≥ 0, there exists an injective function Phi_{m,g}: K_{m,g} → K_{m,g+1}, where K_{m,g} consists of all tuples k=(k_1,...,k_{m-1}) with k_r ∈ Z_{>0} and sum_{r=1}^{m-1} k_r = g, such that for all integers i,j with 1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1: if i+j<m then k_i+k_j ≥ k_{i+j}, and if i+j>m then k_i+k_j+1 ≥ k_{i+j-m} (with no stated constraint when i+j=m).
quantifier_order: For membership k ∈ K_{m,g}: ∀ i,j ∈ Z (1 ≤ i ≤ j ≤ m-1 → [case constraints depending on i+j<m or i+j>m])
∃ Phi_{m,g} (Phi_{m,g} is injective and maps K_{m,g} into K_{m,g+1})

variables.name: m
variables.role: fixed parameter, length parameter for tuples

variables.name: g
variables.role: fixed parameter controlling the sum constraint

variables.name: i
variables.role: index quantifier for membership constraints in K_{m,g}

variables.name: j
variables.role: index quantifier for membership constraints in K_{m,g}

variables.name: Phi_{m,g}
variables.role: injective map whose existence is asserted

witness_dependencies: Phi_{m,g} is allowed to depend on the fixed parameters (m,g)

For every k ∈ K_{m,g}, the output Phi_{m,g}(k) must satisfy the defining constraints of K_{m,g+1} (in particular, it must be a (m-1)-tuple of positive integers summing to g+1 and obeying the same i+j<m / i+j>m inequalities)
Injectivity of Phi_{m,g} refers to equality of outputs on distinct inputs within K_{m,g}
